Subject: FintechX - model quality eval follow-up

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really useful discovery. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Priority: reduce hallucinations in financial question-answering and improve consistency on sensitive fields (account numbers, transaction dates).
- Success criteria you mentioned: hallucination rate < 3% on our eval set, and latency under 200ms p50 for single-turn queries.
- Redwood differentiators to validate: model quality parity vs hyperscalers on safety prompts, deterministic fallback routing, and token-level cost breakdown for multi-model A/B.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) We’ll run the eval you shared across two open models + a Redwood-optimized variant and compare hallucination, factuality, and response divergence.
2) I’ll introduce our ML lead (Neha) and SE (Rishi) to coordinate eval parameters and acceptance thresholds.
3) Schedule a results review next week — propose Wed 3/24 10am PT.

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan-v2.pdf (POC plan + suggested tests)

Would you please send the canonical eval prompts/dataset (CSV or JSONL) and any target labeling guidance? You mentioned a curated bank of customer-support Qs — that’d be perfect.

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — good recap. Attaching the eval set we discussed and a short labeling guide. A few clarifications before you run the tests: 

- The eval set (fintechx-eval-set-v1.csv) contains 1,200 user queries + expected canonical answers. We labeled hallucinations as any time the model returns a fabricated account number or a materially incorrect transaction amount/date.
- For safety prompts, we want explicit detection of PII leakage and incorrect system instructions.
- We also want a column indicating "business impact" (high/med/low) for each prompt so you can surface regressions on high-impact examples.

Attachments: fintechx-eval-set-v1.csv, eval-labeling-guidelines.md

I can confirm Wed 3/24 10am PT works — if you can do a 30–45m slot to walk through the results and next experiments that’d be great.

Elena Garcia
Head of Product | FintechX
elena.garcia@fintechx.com

Elena — looping in Neha (ML lead) and Rishi (Solutions Eng) to align on the test plan. Quick notes on the tests we’ll run and questions for you: 

Planned tests (first pass):
- Baseline: run FintechX eval set against Hyperscaler-A (default), Hyperscaler-B (safety-tuned), and Redwood-optimized Llama-variant (quantized where applicable).
- Metrics: hallucination rate (per your labeling guide), factuality precision, top-1 response divergence, avg token cost, latency p50/p95.
- Breakdown by business-impact bucket so we prioritize fixes.

Questions / asks:
1) For hallucination labeling, should we treat partially-correct numerical answers (e.g., correct amount but wrong date) as a hallucination? Our default is yes — flag any materially incorrect field.
2) Do you have an existing threshold for acceptable divergence from canonical answers (e.g., edit distance or semantic similarity cutoff)? If not, we’ll propose 0.8 cosine on sentence-embedding similarity.
3) Are there any model families you explicitly want us to exclude from comparison?

Proposed logistics: run first-pass tests by Tue EOD (3/23). Share initial report Wed morning so we can discuss on the 3/24 call. Rishi — can you confirm we have GPU quota for the Redwood-optimized runs and whether we should use the low-latency config?

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Elena / Marissa,

Quick update from the initial pass (attached: initial-model-quality-report.pdf). High-level: 

- Hallucination rate (as defined in your guide): Hyperscaler-A = 4.8%, Hyperscaler-B = 3.9%, Redwood-optimized = 2.1%. Redwood shows a notable reduction on account-number and transaction-date fabrications.
- Factuality precision (exact match on canonical fields): Hyperscaler-A 88%, Hyperscaler-B 90%, Redwood-optimized 93%.
- Latency (single-turn, low-concurrency): Redwood p50 = 165ms, p95 = 410ms. Hyperscaler p50 ranged 120–180ms depending on region.
- Cost: preliminary token-cost delta ~ Redw vs Hyperscaler-A = -12% (i.e., Redwood is ~12% cheaper on these prompts in current config).

Notes & next steps:
- We recommend a targeted safety tuning pass focused on the high-impact bucket (approx 220 prompts) to push hallucination < 1.5%.
- We also observed a pattern where open models hallucinate when prompts contain nested date ranges; we’ll add targeted synthetic prompts to probe that behaviour.
- If you want us to run deterministic A/B with a hyperscaler variant behind our routing (to measure end-to-end differences including network/infra), we can schedule those runs as a follow-up.

Attachments: initial-model-quality-report.pdf (includes per-prompt breakdown and examples of hallucinations), test-configuration.yaml (test configs)

Elena — would Wed 3/24 still work for a deep dive? I can extend the session to cover tunings and propose the safety-tuning timeline. If not, we can do Thu 3/25 morning.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
